info.description:
Wish Marketplace V3 API # General Information The Wish Marketplace API will be using oAuth to authenticate in order to offer better security for its users * Learn about oAuth [here](oauth). * If you are a merchant and want to create an application for yourself, learn about how to create a private app [here](../../private-app) * If you are a ERP and create applications that'll be used by multiple merchants, learn about how to create a public app [here]( ../../public-app). You will need to apply to be a verified public application ## How to Test To avoid testing the API on production data, use our sandbox. The sandbox is completely contained and will not affect Wish users or your merchant account. To reach the sandbox, visit: https://sandbox.merchant.wish.com. To use the sandbox in testing, use https://sandbox.merchant.wish.com/api/v3/ as your base URL. How to Generate test data after you have created a sandbox account: 1. Navigate to the [unfulfilled orders page](https://sandbox.merchant.wish.com/transactions/action) 2. Hover over the dropdown next to the 'fulfill with csv' button and select Generate Orders ## Date/Time Format All dates and times in our API are returned in the same format. It is in the form `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sss±XX:ZZ` or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ`, where 'Z' represents UTC timezone. When sending timestamps in URL parameters or the request body, millisecond is optional and will defaults to 0 if not provided. * `YYYY` is the year * `MM` is the month * `DD` is the day * `HH` is the hour (in 24-hour clock format) * `mm` is the minutes * `ss.sss` is the seconds and milliseconds * `±XX:ZZ` is the UTC offset of the form +XX:ZZ or -XX:ZZ where XX is a 2-digit string giving the number of UTC offset hours, and ZZ is a 2-digit string giving the number of UTC offset minutes. ## Response Schema Every response returned from the Wish API will have the same schema. This schema is intended to give you a predictable manner to check the status of your request and know where to get the data. Each response will have the following top level attributes: message, code and data. **Attributes**
Message A message describing the error that happened, example: "We could not find a product for id: '5d30f60e0a6fc464f4f376b0'"
Code A unique number which represents the error that has occurred, example: 1008 or 0 if success.
Data For errors this will be empty.
## General Querying Techniques ### Partial Resources All GET endpoints (except OAuth) support a fields parameter which allows for requesting a partial response. Any fields specified in the response schema of an endpoint can be selected. The top level attribute `data` can be ignored when using the fields parameter. **Syntax** * Comma-separated list to select multiple fields * Use forward slash `/` to select nested field: `field1/nested_field` * Use parentheses `( )` to select multiple nested fields: `field1(nested_field1,nested_field2)` * Use `*` for wildcard selection: `field1/nested_field/*` **Example:** ``` https://merchant.wish.com/api/v3/demo/get?fields=title,items(id,info/name) ``` Which would result in the following partial response: ``` { "title": "demo", "items": [ { "id": "1", "info": { "name": "demo_item_1" } }, { "id": "2", "info": { "name": "demo_item_2" } }, ... ] } ``` ## Locale You can optionally specify locale in order to translate content and error messages into your language. To do this use the [Accept-Language](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Accept-Language) header to specify your preferred locales. If none is provided, your default locale will be used. For example, to request content in Chinese use: `Accept-Language: zh` In the response, you will receive a [Content-Language](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Language) header that specifies the locale code of the response content. ## Rate-Limiting Rate-limiting will be performed on a per-merchant basis for each app. It is your responsibility to ensure you are not making frequent unnecessary calls to the API. If the rate limits cannot satisfy your need, we highly recommend integrating webhooks for your app. With webhooks, instead of pulling resources periodically, your app will receive real-time notifications for particular events that occur to a merchant’s store. [Learn more](https://merchant.wish.com/documentation/webhooks) **Normal Usage** To help you track the rate-limiter status, the following response header(s) will be provided with each response: * `Wish-Rate-Limit-Remaining`: The number of calls remaining in the current rate-limiting window. **Rate-Limit Exceeded** After you exceed the number of allowed calls in the current rate-limiting window, you will receive a `429 Too Many Requests` error response and the following additional header(s): * `Wish-Rate-Limit-Reset`: The time the rate-limiter will reset. Once you receive this response there is nothing you can do except wait for the rate-limiter to reset. In order to avoid being rate-limited, you may want to cache your responses. ## Sorting ### Overview Sorting is available for most endpoints that return a collection (list) of objects. Each collection has a different set of enabled parameters for sorting, so please check specific collection section for detail. ### Usage Append `sort_by={parameter_name}.{asc|desc}` in your API request where `parameter_name` is a valid sortable parameter of that endpoint. Example: ``` /api/v3/penalties?sort_by=created_at.asc ``` ## Pagination All bulk-fetching API methods that return lists of resource support pagination. These methods commonly take at least 3 parameters: `limit`, `{attribute}_min`, `{attribute}_max`. Attribute can be `id`, `create_at`, etc., depending on each specific method. For instance, you make a request to get a list of penalties `/api/v3/penalties?limit=20&created_at_max=2020-04-08T23:59:59Z&sort_by=created_at_max.desc`, which means to fetch 20 penalities sorted by their creation time, with the most recent one being created before `2020-04-08T23:59:59Z`. Assume that the response contains 20 `penalty` objects with the last object being `penalty_foo`, then your subsequent request can be `/api/v3/penalties?limit=20&created_at_max={penalty_foo.create_at}&sort_by=created_at_max.desc` to fetch the next page of list. Note that when fetching next page using `id_min` or `id_max`, you need to perform `+/- 1`(correspondingly) on the last object's ID in the current page, as `id_min` and `id_max` are inclusive. (All V3 API resources' IDs are either integer or BSON object ID - a hex number). ## Request ID Each API request is associated with a unique identifier. You can find this value in response headers, under `Wish-Request-Id`. **When you need to contact us about a specific request, please provide this ID to ensure the fastest possible reply** # Authentication For all requests that require OAuth2 authentication, the access token must be provided in the `Authorization` request header in the following format: `Authorization: Bearer ` For example: ``` Authorization: Bearer 3d6e2d71bc464e42bfbdb081afb73c1e ```

UnqualifiedReason.description: Reason of unqualified product variations.</br> 'NOT_IN_STOCK': product out of stock.</br> 'LOW_RATING': product rating is too low (Minimum of 3 for Discount promotions, or 4 for Flash Sale promotions).</br> 'SALE_HISTORY': no product sales in the last 90 calendar days.</br> 'DISCOUNT_PRICE_HISTORY': discounted product price must be lower than or equal to the lowest price in the product's history for the past 30 calendar days.</br> 'PRODUCT_SHIPPING_PRICE': product shipping price cannot be increased before promotion starts.</br> 'PRODUCT_CATEGORY': some product categories are not eligible for the promotion type.</br> 'CAMPAIGN_LIMIT': replaced by COMPETING_PROMOTION and PROMOTION_HISTORY, products cannot be on conflicting campaigns at the same time. Products can only enroll in campaign of the same type 30 calendar days after the previous one ends.</br> 'MINIMUM_VARIATION_PERCENTAGE': all of a product's variations should be included for this promotion type.</br> 'FLASH_SALE_MINIMUM_VARIATION_INVENTORY': A certain percent of variation inventory should be included in the promotion.</br> 'VARIATIONS_PRICING_GAMING': variations' discounts have a steep difference, with most discounts at the lower end of the range.</br> 'PRODUCT_LISTED_DAYS': product must be listed on the platform more than 30 calendar days, and variation must be listed on the platform more than 15 calendar days.</br> 'MERCHANT_ELIGIBILITY': merchant is not eligible to participate in the promotions platform.</br> 'NOT_OWNED_BY_MERCHANT': each variation must be owned by the merchant.</br> 'UNITY_PRODUCT': products in the shipping unification initiative are not currently eligible for promotions.</br> 'INVALID_ID': invalid or nonexistent product or variation ID.</br> 'FRS_LOW_DISCOUNT': after flat rate shipping is applied, the customer's discount is lower than 5%; to fix, the merchant must increase the discount.</br> 'FRS_HIGH_DISCOUNT': after flat rate shipping is applied, the customer's discount is higher than 90%; to fix, the merchant must decrease the discount.</br> 'FRS_DISCOUNT_PRICE': the flat rate shipping rate is greater than the customer's total price for this item after discount; to fix, the merchant must decrease the discount.</br> 'FRS_NEGATIVE_PRICE': after flat rate shipping is applied, the promotion discount results in a negative return on the product price; to fix, the merchant must decrease the discount percentage.</br> 'COMPETING_PROMOTION': products cannot be in two or more promotions running at the same time.</br> 'PROMOTION_HISTORY': products cannot enroll in a promotion of the same type (e.g., Discount, Flash Sale) within 5 calendar days after a previous promotion ends.</br> 'NEGATIVE_PRODUCT_PRICE': The promotion discount results in a negative product price; to fix, the merchant must decrease the discount percentage.</br> 'LOW_RATING_COUNT': product rating count is too low (Minimum of 1).</br> 'PRODUCT_NOT_ACTIVE': product is either removed or pending/rejected on review.

tax_information.description: This attribute returns information relevant to an order's tax requirements

refunds.description: Returns relevant information regarding all of an order's refunds

total_frs_quantity.description: The total quantity of FRS items within the transaction of this order.

special_programs.description: Returns all special programs associated with this order.

fulfillment_order_types.description:
Returns the various programs this order can be a part of:

1. WISH_EXPRESS: Wish Express
2. FULFILLED_BY_WISH: Fulfilled by Wish
3. FULFILLED_BY_STORE: Fulfilled by Store
4. LESS_THAN_TRUCKLOAD: Less-than-Truckload
5. PREMIUM_SHIPPING_CARRIER_UPGRADE: Premium Shipping Carrier Upgrade
6. ADVANCED_LOGISTICS: Advanced Logistics
7. OPTIONAL_ADVANCED_LOGISTICS: Optional Advanced Logistics
8. CONFIRMED_DELIVERY_POLICY: Confirmed Delivery Policy
9. VAT: Value-added Tax
10. PC_VAT: Pay Customer VAT
11. UNIFICATION_INITIATIVE: Unification Initiative
12. MAX_DELIVERY_DAY_REQUIREMENT: Merchant-set Time To Door
13. CALCULATED_SHIPPING: Calculated Shipping
14. WISH_PLUS: Wish Plus Order

If an order is a part of multiple programs  (ex: FULFILLED_BY_WISH & Wish Express), the output will be a combination of the relevant enums (ex: WISH_EXPRESS,FULFILLED_BY_WISH)

all.description: The number of views for this video on the given date.

engaged.description: The number of engaged views for this video, where view time was >= 4s or a user action was taken on the given date.

GermanyProductComplianceStatusResponse.description: List of objects including a product id, compliance status and EPR number id.

PromotionsCampaignCancelComment.description: A detailed reason for the campaign cancellation. Used by Wish to collect feedbacks.

FranceProductUniqueIdentificationNumber.description: details of a france product unique identification number

category.description: The enum representing the product category with which the UIN is associated.

uin.description: The unique identification number(UIN) provided by the merchant

product_responsibility_organization.description: The name of the UIN provided by the merchant

Locale.description: A language tag (which is sometimes referred to as a 'locale identifier'). This consists of a 2-3 letter base language tag representing the language, optionally followed by additional subtags separated by '-'. The most common extra information is the country or region variant (like 'en-US' or 'fr-CA'). For more information, see specification [BCP 47](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/bcp47#section-2).

description.description: Description of the specific rule that must be followed when shipping the order

average.description: The average watch time for this video on the given date.

total.description: The total watch time for this video on the given date.

PromotionType.description: Promotion type of the campaign.</br> 'DISCOUNT' campaigns support basic discount on variations.</br> 'FLASH_SALE' campaigns support significant discount on products for a short period of time with limited inventories.

VATAmount.description: Currently only for UK-bound orders; This field breaks down VAT quantities for this order.

shipping_level_vat.description: VAT applied for all shipping within this order (if applicable)

final_vat.description: VAT applied to the total order. This quantity is equal to the sum of VAT applied to both shipping & products.

product_level_vat.description: VAT applied to all products within this order (if applicable)
